hint.text: Persia was an ancient kingdom in the area of modern-day Iran. It was one of the oldest civilisations in human history.
hint.label: Persia

atoms.b: In 499 BC, a few of the eastern Greek city-states began to ((++rebel regal)) against the Persian king, Darius I, who had conquered them.
These states asked ((++Athens Apple)) for help in the fight, and they received a fleet of ((++ships chips)). This came to be known as the Ionian Revolt.

feedback.finish: The Ionian Revolt failed, but it proved that when the Greeks worked together, they could be very powerful. For King Darius, this was a problem.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: In 490 BC, Darius I decided he had to invade the Greek states to remove the threat their fleet posed.

The first main battle between the Greeks and the Persians was the Battle of Marathon, where 10,000 Greeks fought off 20,000 Persians. The Greek stories claimed that they killed 6,400 Persians and only lost 192 Greeks.

The Greeks managed to win the battle by using the terrain well. By fighting in the swamps and mountains, they stopped the Persians from using their famous horsemen and fought in conditions they were more used to.

feedback.finish: One very famous story about the Battle of Marathon mentions a soldier named Pheidippides. He was sent back to Athens to deliver news about the Greek victory.
Pheidippides supposedly ran 26 miles to deliver the news and died upon completing his report! This story inspired the long-distance races, called marathons, that people still run today.
